ومعنى ذِي الذِّكْرِ أي: صاحب الذكر، وكلمة الذكر تُطلَق على معانٍ عدة (...)

Fine-tuning the translation is not needed here; let me translate accurately.

The meaning of "dhi al-dhikr" (ذِي الذِّكْرِ) is: possessor of the Remembrance (dhikr). The word dhikr is applied to several meanings.

So the word dhikr is applied to the noble Qur'an, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed, indeed you are mad!"﴾ [al-Hijr: 6]. The word dhikr is also applied to the books of the earlier messengers, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 43].

The word dhikr is applied to renown and reputation, as came in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you are going to be questioned﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44], meaning: the Qur'an.

And in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We have certainly sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder...﴾ [al-Anbiya': 10]. The Arabs were not exalted, nor was their language elevated, except because it is the language of the Qur'an.

The word dhikr is also applied to remembrance (recollection), as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But Satan made him forget the remembrance of his Lord...﴾ [Yusuf: 42].

The word dhikr is applied to glorification (tasbih), as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings, by men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Nur: 36-37].

The word dhikr is applied to another meaning, namely, the good gift from Allah and the obedient deed of the servant.

So the word dhikr in the Qur'an is like a diamond gleaming in your hand: whenever you turn it, you find it sparkling. All these meanings fall under His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Sad. By the Qur'an, full of reminder.﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 38, verse 2:

We know that (bal) is a particle that expresses either retraction from what precedes it (idrab) or the negation of what precedes it and the affirmation of what follows it. So (bal) here affirms that those who disbelieve are in arrogance and opposition. What, then, is the negated element before it? Before it is His, the Exalted, saying:

﴿Sad. By the Qur'an, full of reminder.﴾

This is the miracle of Muhammad (ﷺ), and it was obligatory that they be convinced by it and believe in it, but they disbelieved. So the meaning is: "Rather, those who disbelieve did not affirm it; rather, they are in arrogance and opposition..."

And the meaning of "fi 'izzah" (in arrogance) is: the arrogance of sin, which is haughtiness and pride toward the truth, and it is an arrogance without any basis.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 38, verse 3:

(Kam) here is khabariyyah (a declarative form of "how many"), indicating abundance. It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, left it to the addressee to imagine the quantity and to specify the quantity with kam. You do not use this style unless you are certain of this abundance, as when you say to someone who denies your favour: "Kam a'taytuka (how much I have given you) or kam sabartu 'alayka (how much I have endured for you)," meaning: many times.

And al-Qarn (the generation), we have said, is a period or group of time governed by one distinguished figure, such as a prophet or other, just as we say "the people of Noah" or "the people of Hud." It has been established that a qarn is one hundred years, and it was called qarn because its years are close (muqaranah) to one another.

In the words of His, exalted is He, ﴿min qablihim﴾ [Sad: 3] there is a fine precaution, because after the mission of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah did not destroy a people in its entirety as happened before him (ﷺ). Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, addressed His Messenger Muhammad with His words: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ [al-Anfal: 33].

So His words, exalted is He, ﴿min qablihim﴾ [Sad: 3] mean: this is a matter that preceded and will not be repeated in the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ). You find a parallel to this matter in His words, exalted is He: ﴿Why then did you kill the prophets of Allah before?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 91].

Had the Truth, glory be to Him, not said (min qablu), the Messenger of Allah might have thought that his people could have killed him as the prophets before him had been killed. But the Truth, glory be to Him, reassures His Messenger with His words ﴿min qablu﴾ [al-Baqarah: 91], meaning: be at ease, this will not be repeated. In this there is a strengthening of his heart (ﷺ).

As for His words, exalted is He, ﴿fa-nadaw﴾ [Sad: 3], meaning: at the moment the punishment descended upon them and general destruction fell upon them, they called out a general call to anyone who hears, to rescue them, relieve them and deliver them. But whom do they call? The Qur'an did not specify the one called, to indicate the terror they were in. Therefore we find that calling out in terror to one who can rescue you from what you cannot withstand has stages proportionate to the danger you face. If someone throws a stone at you, for example, you call upon your own self and summon a part of you, so you move your hand, for instance, or your foot, to avoid the harm.

If the danger is beyond your capacity, you call upon the people nearest to you: your father, your mother, your brother, your neighbour, whoever is walking with you in the street, and so on. If you find no helper among these, you say "ya huwa" (O He). We have said that it means "Ya Huwa," meaning: O Allah, I have none other than You to call upon and to turn to.

When destruction descended upon these people, they called out a general call to anyone able to rescue and relieve them. But far-fetched it is: who can rescue them if what descends upon them is from Allah? Therefore their calling is of no use: ﴿fa-nadaw wa-lata hina manas﴾ [Sad: 3]. The word (lata) is formed from the negation particle la with a ta added to it. La negates in general: it may negate a person, as when you say "la rajula fi al-dar (there is no man in the house)," or negate a place, as when you say "la dara askunuha (there is no house I may dwell in)." When the ta is added, it negates time specifically. Therefore it is followed by the word (hin), like tham and thamma. The poet said:

Thumma'a qumna ila jurdin musawwamatin  a'rafuhunna li-aydina manadilu

And the meaning of (manas) is: escape and refuge. So the meaning of ﴿fa-nadaw wa-lata hina manas﴾ [Sad: 3] is: this is not the time for escape or refuge.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on surah 38, verse 4:

Al-'ajab is astonishment (istighrab). They wonder, but their situation is more wondrous: they wonder ﴿that there has come to them a warner from among themselves; and the disbelievers say, "This is a sorcerer, a great liar."﴾ [Sad: 4]. What is truly wondrous is that a messenger should come to them from a kind other than their own, which is why the Exalted says in another place: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them, except that they said, "Has God sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 94].

They wanted the messenger to be an angel. Yet even if an angel had come to them, he would have come in the form of a man from among them, and if he had appeared to them in the form of a man, doubt would have remained. The Truth, glory be to Him, answers them: ﴿Say: Had there been in the earth angels walking about securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.﴾ [al-Isra': 95]

And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them about what they confuse.﴾ [al-An'am: 9]

So it must be that the one sent is of the same kind as those to whom he is sent, because the messenger is the bearer of a method that he embodies; the messenger is a model and an exemplar for his people. How could the model be realised in an angel? Indeed, had the messenger come as an angel, they would have objected to him, saying that he is an angel, sinless, able to do what we cannot do; moreover, an angel has no desires like ours... etc.

Therefore: the wonder lies in the astonishment that the messenger should be one of them and of their kind. That the messenger be from among you is the proof, and through it the exemplary model is complete. Therefore, when God bestows His favour upon the community of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, He says: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves...﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128], meaning: of your kind, not a stranger to you. This is a privilege for you; so your wonder has no place.

The kind here is not merely the human kind; rather, it is of their own type, the Arabs, and indeed of their noblest, namely the Quraysh. You know him before his mission; you know his origin and lineage. Therefore God answers them, saying: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them...﴾ [Yunus: 15], meaning: plainly clear, undeniable. ﴿Those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it." Say: "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I follow only what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day."﴾ "Say: Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it. I have dwelt among you a lifetime before it. Will you not reason?"" [Yunus: 15–16].

Indeed, our master, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived among his people for forty years before his mission, and they knew everything about him. Therefore the wonder is in the opposite; it is not in the reality they are amazed by.

Then the Truth relates their words: ﴿And the disbelievers say, "This is a sorcerer, a great liar."﴾ [Sad: 4] The sorcerer is one who makes us imagine things so that we see them other than they are, but he does not change the reality. Sorcery is not in the thing itself, but in the eyes of people, as the Exalted says: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people...﴾ [al-A'raf: 116].

Therefore there is a difference between sorcery and the miracle of our master Moses, peace be upon him. It was of a kind that resembles sorcery, since sorcerers opposed him; when Moses threw down his staff and the sorcerers saw it swallowing what they had faked, they said, "We believe in the Lord of Moses." They did this only because they were certain that what Moses brought was not of the category of sorcery. They knew sorcery well and knew the tricks of the sorcerers, and this was not among them.

They see a serpent swallowing what they fabricate, whereas a sorcerer sees things as they really are: he sees ropes as ropes, while people see them as serpents writhing and moving. Thus what Moses did before them was not sorcery.

We answer those who accuse the Messenger of God of sorcery, and we say: Even if we grant you that Muhammad is a sorcerer, and that he bewitched those who believed in him, how is it that you still persist in your disbelief? Why has Muhammad not bewitched you as he bewitched the believers, so that the matter would be settled between you and him?

Then they say: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ [Sad: 5] They wonder and deny that the Messenger of God calls them to monotheism, and to worshipping God alone without partner. They used to worship many gods: there were many idols around the House, and some of them worshipped the sun, the moon, or the planets and stars, and some worshipped the angels, etc.

But from where did this doubt come to them? It came from their magnifying of existence. This marvellous, well-ordered cosmos contains an earth with rivers, mountains, crops and fruits, and a heaven containing sun, moon, stars, planets and orbits, etc. In their view, this cosmos cannot be created by one alone; surely many must have shared in its creation.

Therefore, it is the greatness of existence that led them to speak of multiple gods. Here we must say: Glory be to God! The reverse is true in this matter: the greatness of creation is proof that the Creator is one. Had the Creator been many, creation would not have come in this order and harmony. Had the Creator been many, the situation would be as the Truth, glory be to Him, described: ﴿Otherwise, each god would have taken away what he created, and some would have overcome others...﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 91].

So their saying ﴿Has he made the gods into one God...?﴾ [Sad: 5] is wrong in two respects. The first is their assumption that the greatness of the work is proof of a plurality of the maker, whereas the greatness of the work is proof that the maker is one. The second is that you have said there are many gods, and god (ilah) means the worshipped one whose commands and prohibitions are obeyed. So tell us: by what did these gods command you, and from what did they forbid you? Moreover, what reward have they prepared for those who obey them, and what have they prepared for those who disobey them?

Therefore, your saying "gods" is a lie and nonsense that you utter with your tongues, for which God has sent down no authority. Had you known the meaning of divinity (ilah) and the meaning of worship, and that the one worshipped must have a method by which his servants walk, you would not have spoken of many gods.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, sets forth an example for them, saying: ﴿God presents an example: a man in whom are partners quarrelling, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are the two alike in comparison?...﴾ [al-Zumar: 29].

That is: are the two alike in servitude, the slave owned by one master and the slave owned by several masters? And those masters are not in agreement; rather, they are contentious and disagree among themselves. Likewise, one who worships God alone and one who worships many gods are not alike.

As for their saying ﴿Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ [Sad: 5]: in the preceding verse the Exalted said ﴿and they wondered﴾ [Sad: 4], from the verb 'ajiba, whose verbal noun is 'ajaban. Here, however, He said ('ujab). This form indicates intensification of wonder and astonishment: the root of the verbal noun and its pattern are present in it, and the added length indicates intensity, as we say: tawil and tuwal (long), and amr gharib and gharab (a very strange matter).

Then they say: "Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a astonishing thing." They are amazed at and deny that the Messenger of Allah calls them to monotheism, and to worshipping Allah alone, without partner, when they used to worship many gods: around the House there were many idols, and among them were those who worshipped the sun, or the moon, or the planets and stars, and among them those who worshipped the angels... etc.

But from where did this doubt come to them? This doubt came from their magnifying of existence. This wondrous, perfectly ordered cosmos contains an earth with rivers, mountains, crops and fruits, and contains a heaven with sun, moon, stars, planets and spheres... etc. In their view, this universe cannot be created by one alone; many must have shared in creating it.

So: it is the greatness of existence that led them to speak of multiple gods. Here we must say "Glory be to Allah!" The opposite is the truth in this matter. The greatness of creation is proof that the Creator is one. Had the Creator been many, creation would not have come in this order and harmony. And had the Creator been many, the situation would be as the Real, glorified is He, described it: ﴿Since then each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overcome others﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 91].

So their saying "Has he made the gods into one God?" is wrong from two angles. The first: their assumption that the greatness of a craft is proof of the plurality of the craftsman, whereas the greatness of a craft is proof that the craftsman is one. The second: you say there are many gods, while "ilah" (god) means the worshipped one whose commands and prohibitions are obeyed. So tell us: what have these gods commanded you, and what have they forbidden you? Rather, what reward have they prepared for those who obey them, and what have they prepared for those who disobey them?

So: your saying "gods" is a lie and nonsense that you utter with your tongues, for which Allah has sent down no authority. Had you known the meaning of "god" and the meaning of worship, and that the one worshipped must have a method that his servants follow, you would not have said there are many gods.

Therefore the Real, glorified is He, sets forth an example for them, saying: ﴿Allah sets forth an example: a man in whom are partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are the two equal in comparison?﴾ [al-Zumar: 29].

That is: is one who is a slave owned by a single master equal to a slave owned by several masters, and those masters are not in agreement but quarrel and differ among themselves? Likewise, one who worships Allah alone is not equal to one who worships many gods.

The Notables (al-Mala') are those who fill the eye with awe, appearance and fine dress, and who fill the seats of assemblies. What is meant is the dignitaries, the chiefs of the people and the stubborn leaders of disbelief among the Quraysh, headed by al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Abu Jahl, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Umayya ibn Khalaf, Utba ibn Rabi'a and his brother Shayba, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. God singled them out for mention because they were the people of leadership, and the call of His Messenger (ﷺ) was going to pull the carpet of leadership from under their feet, so they were the ones harmed by the call of the Messenger of God.

There is a story behind this matter. These chiefs went to Abu Talib, the uncle of the Messenger of God, and said to him: "If your nephew wants sovereignty, we will make him king over us; and if he wants wealth, we will gather wealth for him until he becomes the richest of us... etc." So Abu Talib spoke to the Messenger of God and said: "O nephew, spare me and yourself, and do not burden me with a matter I cannot bear. Your people came to me and said such-and-such." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) then made his well-known statement. When their effort failed, and they knew that the Messenger of God would not compromise with them regarding their gods, nor accept their offers and bargaining, they hurried to their people, urging them to hold fast to their gods and to be patient with them: ﴿And the Notables among them went forth﴾ [Sad: 6], meaning: to their people, ﴿saying: "Walk on, and be steadfast for your gods"﴾ [Sad: 6], meaning: continue on what you are upon of worshipping idols, and keep to your way and your worship. ﴿and be steadfast for your gods﴾ [Sad: 6], meaning: in their worship, and beware lest Muhammad lead you astray from them.

﴿Indeed, this is a thing that is intended﴾ [Sad: 6], i.e., a matter that is planned and has consequences that follow it, for if you disbelieve in the gods, they will be angry with you and drought and famine will befall you; or, "the thing is intended against us, the notables, so that we become humbled after having been leaders, and become equal with the rest of the people."

And their saying: ﴿We have not heard of this in the latest religion﴾ [Sad: 7], i.e., we have not heard that God is one. The "latest religion" (al-Milla al-Akhira) is the closest of the religions to them, and it is Judaism and Christianity. Indeed, Judaism and Christianity were sent down from heaven with the monotheism of God, but what encouraged them in this statement is that the Jews said: "Uzayr is the son of God," and the Christians said: "The Messiah is the son of God," and they said: "God is the third of three." Therefore the disbelievers of Mecca said: we have not heard of the oneness of God in the latest religion. ﴿This is nothing but a fabrication﴾ [Sad: 7], meaning: this is nothing but lies and invention. The meaning of al-Ikhtilaq (fabrication) is the creating of a thing without any reality supporting it.

Their saying: "We have not heard of this in the latter religion." That is, we have not heard that God is one. The "latter religion" is the closest of the religions to them, namely Judaism and Christianity. Yes, Judaism and Christianity were sent down from heaven with the oneness of God, but what encouraged them in this saying is that the Jews said, "Ezra is the son of God," and the Christians said, "The Messiah is the son of God," and they said, "God is the third of three." Therefore the disbelievers of Makkah said: we have not heard of the oneness of God in the latter religion. ﴿This is nothing but a fabrication﴾. That is, this is nothing but lies and invention. The meaning of ikhtilaq (fabrication) is: the making up of a thing with no reality supporting it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 38, verse 8:

أَءُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ مِن بَيْنِنَا بَلْ هُمْ فَي شَكٍّ مِّن ذِكْرِي بَل لَّمَّا يَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِ

This is another stage in their dispute and their denial of the Messenger of Allah. Previously they had objected to the Messenger being a human being and had demanded that the Messenger be an angel. Now they abandon this principle and shift to the person himself, as Allah the Exalted says elsewhere: ﴿They said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from one of the two cities?"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31].

Meaning: Why Muhammad specifically, when among us there are great people and chieftains who were more deserving of prophethood than him? And here they said: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?﴾ So Allah, glorified is He, responds to them:

﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 32], thus making his prophethood, peace and blessings be upon him, a mercy to them.

﴿It is We who have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in degrees, so that some of them may take others in service.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 32].

Meaning: How do you interfere in this important matter, wanting to divide the mercy of Allah, when Allah is the One who has apportioned to you the affairs of this worldly life, which are minor, making some of you masters and others slaves, rich and poor, and so on? If the Exalted is the One who arranges for you even the simplest affairs of your lives, how do you hope to divide the grace and mercy of Allah yourselves?

﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124], and that is the grace of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Rather, they are in doubt about My Reminder﴾. The "Reminder" here means the Qur'an, and it is as if the Exalted Lord is consoling His Messenger and comforting his heart, just as He addressed him in another place saying: ﴿We certainly know that what they say saddens you, but it is not you they deny; rather, the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah.﴾ [al-An'am: 33]

The meaning: Do not grieve, O Muhammad. Your people do not deny you; they deny what you have brought of the Reminder. You are, in their eyes, the truthful and trustworthy one against whom there is no blemish. That is to say, the matter does not concern you and your person; it concerns Me. Thus Allah, the Exalted, has taken it from His Messenger's shoulders to reassure him, console him, and lighten for him what he meets of his people's obstinacy toward him.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment﴾. This is a kind of threat, meaning: They will not remain in this state of safety and deliverance, for their punishment is coming. That is because (لما, lamma) indicates the negation of an event in the past together with the affirmation that it will occur in the future. You say: "Fulan has not come" (lam ya'ti), meaning in the past, and he may not come in the present or future; but "Fulan has not yet come" (lamma ya'ti), meaning he has not come in the past, and he will come in the present or future. So the meaning of lamma yadhuqu 'adhabi is: until now the punishment of Allah has not befallen them, but it will certainly befall them.

Following the statement that God, glorified and exalted is He, denied them the ability to distribute His mercy, He here negates that the keys to the treasuries of His mercy are in their hands. So "أم" here is for equalization, and the meaning is: "Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord, or do they have the treasuries of His mercy?" Neither this nor that, because prophethood is mercy, and the treasuries of mercy belong to the Merciful, and God is Ar-Rahman, so they have none of that. For God, exalted is He, has not granted the keys of His treasuries to anyone, not even the close friends (awliya') of God...

The Aziz (the Mighty) is the One who overcomes and is not overcome. God is the Victorious, who is not overcome in His command. And one whose attribute is this, how could they take from Him the treasuries of His mercy? And He, glorified is He, is al-Wahhab (the Bestower), who bestows upon whomever He wills out of His grace and generosity, glorified is He.

Having negated their ability to apportion His mercy, the Truthful (Exalted is He) now negates that the keys to the treasuries of His mercy are in their hands. Here "am" (أم) serves for equalization, and the meaning is: "Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord, or do they have the treasuries of His mercy?" Neither this nor that, because prophethood is mercy, and the treasuries of mercy belong to the Merciful, and Allah is the Most Merciful (al-Rahman). They have no share of that at all, for Allah, Exalted is He, has not given ownership of the keys of His treasuries to anyone, not even to the close friends of Allah (awliya' Allah al-muqarrabun), to whom He grants illuminating, unseen flashes by which certainty is established along the path they have traveled.

Even these He has not made owners of the keys of His treasuries. Rather, He opens for them whatever He wills of His bounty, and gives them what they desire of marvels (karamat), while the keys of His treasuries remain in His hand: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen﴾ [al-An'am: 59], which He never hands over to anyone. Therefore the verse is concluded with two of His names: ﴿the Almighty, the Bestower﴾ [Sad: 9].

The Almighty (al-'Aziz) is the One who prevails and is not overcome; Allah is the Victorious, not overcome in His command. Whoever has this attribute, how could they take from Him the treasuries of His mercy? And He, Exalted is He, is al-Wahhab (the Bestower) [Sad: 9], who gives to whomever He wills out of His grace and generosity, Exalted is He.

Then He, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Or is there for them the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them?﴾ [Sad: 10], meaning: if they had the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, ﴿then let them ascend by the means﴾ [Sad: 10], that is, let them climb up to the sky and ascend to it, so that they themselves may take charge of the management of creation. Allah, Exalted is He, clarifies this matter in another verse: ﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except with authority﴾ [al-Rahman: 33], that is, with authority from Us.

Therefore, when man reached and ascended onto the surface of the moon, the philosophers said: "They arrived by the authority of knowledge." But how, when Allah says after it: ﴿There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and smoke, and you will not be victorious﴾ [al-Rahman: 35]? So the authority intended is not the authority of knowledge as they claim, but authority from Allah, the One who created it. He, Exalted is He, is the One who permits passage to whomever He wills, and prevents passage for whomever He wills. Had this verse not come, those who deny the ascension (mi'raj) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would have been correct.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿A host defeated there, of the confederates﴾ [Sad: 11], the intended ones are the disbelievers of Makkah, and that they will certainly be defeated, just as those before them who denied the messengers were defeated.

Then Allah, Exalted and Glorified is He, consoles His Prophet by mentioning what happened of the denial of the earlier peoples toward their messengers, meaning: O Muhammad, you are not an innovator in this matter. He begins with the longest-lived of the messages, which is the message of our master Noah (peace be upon him), so He, Exalted is He, says:

﴿The people of Noah denied before them...﴾.

Having negated their ability to apportion His mercy, the Truthful (Exalted is He) now negates that the keys to the treasuries of His mercy are in their hands. Here "am" (أم) serves for equalization, and the meaning is: "Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord, or do they have the treasuries of His mercy?" Neither this nor that, because prophethood is mercy, and the treasuries of mercy belong to the Merciful, and Allah is the Most Merciful (al-Rahman). They have no share of that at all, for Allah, Exalted is He, has not given ownership of the keys of His treasuries to anyone, not even to the close friends of Allah (awliya' Allah al-muqarrabun), to whom He grants illuminating, unseen flashes by which certainty is established along the path they have traveled.

Even these He has not made owners of the keys of His treasuries. Rather, He opens for them whatever He wills of His bounty, and gives them what they desire of marvels (karamat), while the keys of His treasuries remain in His hand: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen﴾ [al-An'am: 59], which He never hands over to anyone. Therefore the verse is concluded with two of His names: ﴿the Almighty, the Bestower﴾ [Sad: 9].

The Almighty (al-'Aziz) is the One who prevails and is not overcome; Allah is the Victorious, not overcome in His command. Whoever has this attribute, how could they take from Him the treasuries of His mercy? And He, Exalted is He, is al-Wahhab (the Bestower) [Sad: 9], who gives to whomever He wills out of His grace and generosity, Exalted is He.

Then He, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Or is there for them the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them?﴾ [Sad: 10], meaning: if they had the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, ﴿then let them ascend by the means﴾ [Sad: 10], that is, let them climb up to the sky and ascend to it, so that they themselves may take charge of the management of creation. Allah, Exalted is He, clarifies this matter in another verse: ﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except with authority﴾ [al-Rahman: 33], that is, with authority from Us.

Therefore, when man reached and ascended onto the surface of the moon, the philosophers said: "They arrived by the authority of knowledge." But how, when Allah says after it: ﴿There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and smoke, and you will not be victorious﴾ [al-Rahman: 35]? So the authority intended is not the authority of knowledge as they claim, but authority from Allah, the One who created it. He, Exalted is He, is the One who permits passage to whomever He wills, and prevents passage for whomever He wills. Had this verse not come, those who deny the ascension (mi'raj) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would have been correct.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿A host defeated there, of the confederates﴾ [Sad: 11], the intended ones are the disbelievers of Makkah, and that they will certainly be defeated, just as those before them who denied the messengers were defeated.

Then Allah, Exalted and Glorified is He, consoles His Prophet by mentioning what happened of the denial of the earlier peoples toward their messengers, meaning: O Muhammad, you are not an innovator in this matter. He begins with the longest-lived of the messages, which is the message of our master Noah (peace be upon him), so He, Exalted is He, says:

﴿The people of Noah denied before them...﴾.

Meaning of: ﴿Dhū al-awtād﴾ [Sad: 12]: the possessor of the stakes (awtād), which are fixed things. It is said that the intended meaning is the pyramids. Or he had fixed stakes with which he tortured his opponents. And ﴿al-Aykah﴾ [Sad: 13] is the garden with densely interlaced trees and intertwined branches, and the People of the Aykah (al-Aykah, a thicket of trees) are the people of our master Shu'ayb.

﴿Ulā'ika al-aḥzāb﴾ [Sad: 13], i.e., those who formed factions against their messengers, confronted them, and opposed them stubbornly.

﴿In kullun illā kadhdhaba al-rusul﴾ [Sad: 14]: none of these people did other than deny his messenger. ﴿Fa-ḥaqqa﴾ [Sad: 14], i.e., it became due for him and it was incumbent upon him ('iqāb, punishment). So, how do they imagine for themselves that they may take this stance toward you, O Muhammad, and we will not punish them? How will they escape from us when we have punished those who were stronger than them?

Meaning of: ﴿Dhū al-awtād﴾ [Sad: 12]: the possessor of the stakes (awtād), which are fixed things. It is said that the intended meaning is the pyramids. Or he had fixed stakes with which he tortured his opponents. And ﴿al-Aykah﴾ [Sad: 13] is the garden with densely interlaced trees and intertwined branches, and the People of the Aykah (al-Aykah, a thicket of trees) are the people of our master Shu'ayb.

﴿Ulā'ika al-aḥzāb﴾ [Sad: 13], i.e., those who formed factions against their messengers, confronted them, and opposed them stubbornly.

﴿In kullun illā kadhdhaba al-rusul﴾ [Sad: 14]: none of these people did other than deny his messenger. ﴿Fa-ḥaqqa﴾ [Sad: 14], i.e., it became due for him and it was incumbent upon him ('iqāb, punishment). So, how do they imagine for themselves that they may take this stance toward you, O Muhammad, and we will not punish them? How will they escape from us when we have punished those who were stronger than them?

Verse 14: "Each of them did nothing but deny the Messengers, so My punishment became due." (Tafsir: "Each of them" refers to these people.)

Al-Sha'rawi: "No one of these people but denied his Messenger, so it became due for him, and it became due upon him (punishment)." So: how do they imagine for themselves that they can stand against you, O Muhammad, in this position, and We will not punish them? How will they escape from Us, when We have punished those who were stronger than them?

What they are awaiting is, relative to Us, a trivial matter that requires no treatment; it is merely a single cry, that is, one single blast. They said: it is the second blast by which creation will be resurrected. ﴿Not a single pause (fawaq) will it have﴾ [Sad: 15], meaning: there will be no respite (ifaqa) for them after it.

Meaning of ﴿qittana﴾ [Sad: 16]: i.e., our share and our reward. Its origin is from "qit'ah" (a piece), for they used to write the prize on it. The meaning is: if we are sinners, hasten for us the punishment now, before the Day of Resurrection. But how could the punishment come upon you now in this world, when the world is perishing? Punishment ends with its perishing, so their punishment in this world does not suffice as a recompense for their disbelief. Therefore Allah delays it for them until the Day of Resurrection, which is the abode of lasting and permanence, having no end.

The truth is that the Blast is not what will punish them; rather, it is merely a bell announcing the beginning of this Day.

The Exalted and Glorified explains and clarifies this attitude of theirs in His saying: ﴿And when they said: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ [al-Anfal: 32].

This is evidence of their stupidity: would any sensible person pray for such a thing? It is as if the Exalted wants to show us that their stance of obstinacy and refusal of the messages works against their own souls: instead of saying, "Guide us to it," they say, ﴿Then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [al-Anfal: 32].

Therefore the Exalted marvels at their hastening of the punishment: ﴿Then is it Our punishment that they seek to hasten? * But when it descends upon their courtyard, evil will be the morning of those who were warned﴾ [as-Saffat: 176-177].

It is strange of the disbelievers of Makkah that they say, ﴿before the Day of Reckoning﴾ [Sad: 16]. Do they believe in this Day? If so, why do they utter it and acknowledge its existence, so that it appears in the slips of their tongues? It is said: it is the awakening of the intuitions of the innate nature (fitrah) before the cunning intellect begins to work. The one who lies employs his intellect in lying, and he must have a good memory, because falsehood has no fixed reality.

Therefore a person often tells one lie today and tells the opposite tomorrow, for the truthful man's speech does not change, since he narrates a reality, whereas the liar narrates something other than reality. Hence they said: "If you are a liar, then be a person with a good memory." For example, a lying man who says: "We went to the (bandar) on the night of the little feast, and the world was (moonlit!!)... how?"

The skilled investigator is the one who exploits this matter to learn the truth of statements from their falsehood. The truthful man narrates a reality, so if the investigator asked him a thousand times, his statements would come out one and the same; but the liar narrates an imagination, in which his statements are bound to contradict one another, and his falsehood is then exposed. Reality dictates itself upon you, whereas falsehood is dictated by fabrication and forgery, so you do not know in what form it will come.

Thus their saying ﴿before the Day of Reckoning﴾ [Sad: 16] came from them as a slip of the tongue that revealed what they believe in among themselves. Similar to it is the saying of the hypocrites: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 7].

They made utilitarianism the criterion, as if the followers of Muhammad, when nothing is spent on them, will scatter from around him; that is because matters are material in their eyes, and everything has a price for them.

And they said, when revelation paused from the Messenger of Allah: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him." Thus the innate intuitions carry them away, and the truth appears in the slips of the tongue when the instinct and the fitrah are awakened, and the cunning, managing intellect is absent.

Or they said ﴿And they said: "Our Lord, hasten for us our share before the Day of Reckoning"﴾ [Sad: 16] by way of mockery of the threat with which Allah threatened them. They did not believe in this punishment nor trust in its occurrence, so their hastening for it was mockery of it, as if they said: "Bring us the punishment, for we are eager for Your punishment, so do not delay it until the Day of Reckoning." And this mockery does not befit their saying ﴿Our Lord﴾ [Sad: 16].

Patience: the soul's elevation above events, meaning that events do not overpower the soul or its strength. For one who suffers a calamity needs an extra strength beyond his natural strength, so do not let the calamity or hardship weaken your strength to bear the event.

Beware of making one calamity into two, when you weaken before events so that the calamity and the weakness to bear it gather upon you...

Here, the Truth, glorified is He, wants to console His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and lighten for him what he encounters from his people. Their saying about the Messenger of Allah that he is a sorcerer, a liar, a madman, and so on, all of this grieves the Messenger of Allah, distresses him and pains him. Therefore many verses have passed us in consoling him (ﷺ), as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿We certainly know that what they say saddens you, but it is not you they deny; rather, the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah﴾ [al-An'am: 33].

And here his Lord addresses him: ﴿Be patient over what they say﴾, then gives him an example from the procession of the earlier messages: ﴿And remember Our servant Dawud﴾. But why was Prophet Dawud (David) mentioned specifically in this context?

They said: because the people of Prophet Dawud said about him something more grievous than what was said about the Messenger of Allah. The disbelievers of Makkah said: sorcerer, soothsayer, and liar. But the people of Dawud accused him in his honour, chastity and purity, when they claimed that he sent one of his commanders out to war outside the land, because he loved his wife and wanted the way to be clear for him and that he be alone with her. Despite this, Prophet Dawud was patient.

The Truth, glorified is He, addresses His Prophet Muhammad and says to him: be patient as Dawud was patient. Although Muhammad is the Seal of all the Messengers, there is no messenger after him, and Allah delegated to him the authority to legislate for his community, a distinction not granted to any other of the messengers; and Allah sent with him an enduring book, dominating over all the earlier books. Yet his Lord says to him: be patient as Dawud was patient, and as your brothers among the messengers were patient, to show that the community of messages is one community, each of them conveying from Allah a message suited to his people, so the messengers are all like one person.

Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And remember Our servant Dawud﴾, and after that mentioned a number of messengers from the procession of the messages, and did not say "Our servants," as if they were all gathered in one mission, so do not differentiate among them. Therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿He has prescribed for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein...﴾ [ash-Shura: 13].

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not prefer me over Yunus ibn Matta."

Because you do not know the criteria of preference, so leave preference to Allah, the Exalted, for it is He who prefers, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Those messengers — We have preferred some of them over others﴾ [al-Baqarah: 253].

Consider this great honour that Prophet Dawud attained when the Truth spoke of him, saying ﴿And remember Our servant Dawud﴾. Likewise Prophet Muhammad attained it at the opening of Surat al-Isra: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra: 1]. The night journey has no basis other than that he (ﷺ) was a servant who sincerely devoted himself to servitude to Allah, so he deserved this great honour. Therefore, when the people of Ta'if turned against him, persecuted and insulted him, consolation came from Allah: if the earth did not embrace you, the heaven will embrace you.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Dha al-Ayd﴾, it means: possessor of strength in worship. Faith truly requires a strength that helps you in obedience, restrains you from disobedience, and curbs the soul's unruliness when it inclines you toward opposition. As for obedience, it needs strength, because obedience is often burdensome upon the soul, so it needs a driving, motivating force; therefore He, exalted is He, says of it: ﴿And indeed it is hard, except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45].

As for disobedience, it has pleasure, attraction and desires that press upon the soul, so it also needs resolve and a restraining, curbing strength; therefore the mention of strength recurs often in the Book of Allah. He said of Dawud: ﴿Dha al-Ayd﴾, and He said to Yahya, peace be upon him: ﴿O Yahya, take the Book with strength﴾ [Maryam: 12].

The believer must necessarily be strong, strong in will and resolve; he needs the force that pushes him to acts of obedience, because he is lazy toward them, and the force that restrains him from sins, because he inclines toward them. A person grows lax in obedience and does not desire disobedience only when he separates the deed from its recompense and consequence. Had he kept the recompense in mind and remembered the outcome, obedience would become light for him, easy upon his soul, and sins would become hateful to him, and he would flee from them as one flees from a lion...

Then the Exalted says in describing Prophet Dawud: ﴿Indeed he was a constant returner﴾. From the verb āba (to return), āyib, and awwāb is an intensive form on the pattern fa''āl. It means: one who repeats repentance and returning to Allah much. This word contains an indication that man is prone to sin, and that however much he repents he remains exposed to returning again, for he is not infallible. The important thing is that every sin be followed by repentance, and that you not persist in returning to it...

And His saying about Prophet Dawud: ﴿Indeed he was a constant returner﴾ — later He will explain to us the meaning of:

﴿And he fell down bowing and turned in repentance﴾ [Sad: 24].

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 38, verse 18:

Almighty God informs us that inanimate things glorify Him, and that inanimate things have a kind of life. Man thinks that "inanimate" means lifeless and without any life. Yes, it has no life by your measure, but it has another life, different from yours... So... everything has a life particular to itself, and although we do not grasp the true reality (kunh) of this life, it exists, as evidenced by the fact that everything perishes...

When you read about our master Dawud (David): ﴿Indeed, We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with him, in the evening and at dawn﴾, know that the mountains truly glorify, with a glorification that none knows except their Lord and Creator. The distinction here belongs to our master Dawud, not to the glorification of the mountains, for the mountains are always glorifying; rather, the miracle here is that they glorify together with him and repeat with him one single hymn. So the emphasis is on "with him" (ma'ahu), meaning they glorify along with his glorification.

Therefore, when people say, "The pebbles glorified in the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," we said: Correct the expression, because the pebbles glorify even in the hand of Abu Jahl. The correct and miraculous phrasing is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard the glorification of the pebbles in his hand. This is the greatness.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And the birds gathered together, all of them returning to Him in devotion.﴾ The meaning of "gathered" (maḥshūrah) is: assembled around our master Dawud (ʿalayhi al-salām). This is because he (ʿalayhi al-salām) had a beautiful voice when he recited the Psalms (al-Mazāmīr) and sang them, so the birds would gather around him, repeat along with him, and echo what he said. So there was, then, a faith-based system composed of our master Dawud, the mountains, and the birds, all of them repeating one single glorification...

Therefore they said regarding ﴿all of them returning to Him in devotion﴾: that is, Dawud, the mountains, and the birds, each of them is devoted (awwāb) to Allah, submissive to Him and returning to Him.

Patience: the soul's elevation above events, meaning that events do not overcome the self or its strength. The one who suffers a calamity needs strength beyond his natural strength, so do not let calamity or hardship weaken your power to bear the event.

Beware of making one calamity into two, when you weaken before events and so the calamity and the inability to bear it gather upon you. For the believer's calamity is of two kinds. The first: a calamity in which the person has a share, like the negligent student who fails the examination; the failure is the result of your neglect and laxity. If you are going to be angry, then be angry with yourself, blame it and rebuke it, and try to correct its error and set right its corruption. This is manliness that faces reality and does not evade responsibility.

The second: patience over an event in which the person has no share. This is the decree of God which He brings upon you, and He wants for you only good from it, even if you think it is evil.

Therefore a person may supplicate for what he sees as good for him according to his own reckoning and his understanding of good, but he does not see an answer, so he becomes angry and says: "I called upon Him, and He did not answer me." He forgets that his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, knows best where the good lies, and therefore did not answer him. So His answer to you is that He does not answer you.

Therefore the True One, glorified is He, teaches the believers the response to those who used to mock when events befell them, saying: ﴿Say: Nothing will afflict us except what Allah has decreed for us﴾ [al-Tawbah: 51]. Yes, Allah has decreed for us, not against us, for calamity does not come to the believer except with good. It is either a purification for us, or an elevation of our rank, or so that those who are not believers may know that the people of faith have steadfastness before events and a firmness that does not bend.

On the other hand, we find that the calamity which befalls a person is either a calamity in which he has an adversary, or a calamity with no adversary. The calamity in which you have an adversary, one who has wronged you for example, requires a stronger patience, endurance and greater forbearance, because whenever you see your adversary it stirs up the hidden impulses of the soul and the motives of revenge. As for the calamity in which you have no adversary, which is the decreed calamity that has struck you by the decree of Allah, it is easier on the soul than the first, because it is from Allah. So you have nothing to do but say: "There is no power nor might except with Allah," and be patient and seek reward. Otherwise, what would you do, for example, in the face of sickness or death?

Therefore He, glorified is He, says regarding the calamity in which you have an adversary: ﴿But whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [al-Shura: 43]. That is: it requires resolve and a strength of endurance that helps you to be patient, or calls you to forgiveness. As for the decreed calamity in which you have no adversary, the True One says of it: ﴿And be patient over what has afflicted you; indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [Luqman: 17]. He did not say here ﴿indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ with the lam as in al-Shura: 43. The verse of Luqman concerns the calamity with no adversary, so it came without the lam, and the verse of al-Shura, where there is an adversary, came with the lam.

Here the True One wants to console His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and lighten for him what he meets from his people. Their saying about the Messenger of Allah that he is a sorcerer, a liar, a madman, and so on, all of this grieves the Messenger of Allah, distresses him and pains him. Therefore many verses have passed us consoling him (ﷺ), such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We know that what they say grieves you, but it is not you they deny; rather, the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah﴾ [al-An'am: 33].

Here his Lord addresses him: ﴿Be patient over what they say﴾ [Sad: 17], then gives him an example from the procession of the earlier messages: ﴿And remember Our servant Dawud﴾ [Sad: 17]. But why was Dawud mentioned specifically in this context?

They said: because the people of Dawud said about him what was more atrocious than what was said about the Messenger of Allah. The Meccan disbelievers said: sorcerer, soothsayer, liar. But the people of Dawud accused him in his honour, chastity and purity, when they claimed that he sent one of his commanders to a war outside the land, because he loved his wife and wanted the way to be clear for him to be alone with her. Yet Dawud was patient.

The True One addresses His Prophet Muhammad and says to him: be patient as Dawud was patient. Although Muhammad is the Seal of all the Messengers, there is no messenger after him, and Allah delegated to him the legislation for his community, a distinction not granted to any other of the Messengers, and Allah sent with him an eternal book, guardian over all the earlier books, yet his Lord says to him: be patient as Dawud was patient, and as your brothers among the Messengers were patient, to show that the community of messengership is one community, each of them conveys from Allah a message suited to his people, so the Messengers are all like one person.

Therefore He said: ﴿And remember Our servant Dawud﴾ [Sad: 17], and after that He mentioned several Messengers from the procession of messages, and did not say "Our servants," as if they had all gathered in one task, so do not distinguish between them. Therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not divide therein...﴾ [al-Shura: 13].

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not prefer me over the prophets..." Because you do not know the measures of preference, leave preference to Allah, the Exalted, for He is the One who prefers, as He said, glorified is He: ﴿Those messengers, We preferred some of them over others﴾ [al-Baqarah: 253].

Consider the great honour that Dawud attained when the True One spoke of him, saying ﴿And remember Our servant Dawud﴾ [Sad: 17]. Likewise Muhammad attained it at the opening of Surat al-Isra': ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra': 1]. There is no reason for the night journey except that he (ﷺ) was a servant who devoted sincere servitude to Allah, so he deserved this great honour. Therefore when Ta'if turned against him, persecuted him and insulted him, consolation came from Allah: if the earth did not welcome you, the heavens will welcome you.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Dhu al-Ayd﴾ [Sad: 17], it means: possessor of strength in worship. Faith truly requires a strength that helps you to obey, restrains you from disobedience, and bridles the soul when it inclines you toward transgression. Obedience requires strength because obedience is often heavy upon the soul, so it needs a driving, motivating force; therefore He, exalted is He, says of it: ﴿And indeed, it is difficult except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45].

As for disobedience, it has pleasure, attraction and desires that press upon the soul, so it likewise needs resolve and a restraining, checking strength. Therefore the mention of strength recurs often in the Book of Allah. He said of Dawud ﴿Dhu al-Ayd﴾ [Sad: 17], and He said to Yahya, peace be upon him: ﴿O Yahya, take the Book with strength﴾ [Maryam: 12].

So the believer must be strong, strong in will and resolve. He needs the strength that drives him to acts of obedience, because he is lax toward them, and the strength that repels him from sins, because he inclines toward them. A person does not grow lazy about obedience nor desire disobedience except when he separates the deed from its recompense and consequence. Had he kept the reward in mind and remembered the consequence, obedience would have become light for him and easy on his soul, and he would have shunned disobedience and fled from it as one flees from a lion.

We have clarified this matter with an example: suppose a young man is overcome by the sexual instinct, which is the most violent of human instincts. We say to him: you spend a night with a beautiful girl, but in the morning we will put you into this blazing furnace for an hour. What does he say? Therefore, keeping the punishment for sin in mind at the moment of sin prevents you from it, and likewise keeping the reward for obedience in mind drives you to it.

And there in the Himalaya mountains, near the summit of Everest, they found many victims of those who try to climb this peak. Some died a third of the way, some two-thirds, and so on. What moved them to endure these hardships and dangers? It is the desire to stand above this peak, which is considered the highest peak in the world. It is the love of fame and the immortalising of remembrance in encyclopaedias. Therefore they disregarded the dangers to reach this goal they aspired to.

So what makes a person renounce acts of obedience and grow lazy about them is that he has not kept their reward in mind. Had he kept their reward in mind, they would have become easy for him, as the poet said:

Our souls become cheap in the pursuit of lofty things, and whoever seeks the beautiful maiden is not deterred by the bride-price.

And the Prophet (ﷺ) explains this matter to us by his saying: [the hadith]. That is: the description of faith is negated from him at the moment he commits this sin, because he forgot the consequence and forgot Allah, and had he kept Allah in mind he would not have proceeded.

Then the Most High says describing Dawud: ﴿Indeed, he was ever returning [to Allah]﴾ [Sad: 17]. From the verb aba, ya'ibu, and awwab is an intensive form on the pattern fa''al. That is: frequent in repentance and in turning back to Allah. This word contains an indication that man is prone to disobedience, and that however much he repents he is still liable to return again, because he is not infallible. The important thing is that every sin be followed by repentance, and that you not persist in returning to it.

Therefore you notice that among the names of Allah is al-Ghaffar: ﴿And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, does righteousness, and then remains guided﴾ [Ta-Ha: 82]. He did not say Ghafir. Why? Because creation has heedlessness, and disobedience that recurs, and recurring disobedience requires recurring forgiveness. Therefore it is of Allah's mercy toward us that He is Ghaffar, that is, abundant in forgiveness.

His saying, exalted is He, concerning Dawud: ﴿Indeed, he was ever returning﴾ [Sad: 17] is explained later by the meaning of ﴿and he fell down bowing and turned in repentance﴾ [Sad: 24].

Then the Most High says: ﴿Indeed, We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with him in the evening and at sunrise﴾ [Sad: 18]. The meaning of ﴿in the evening﴾ [Sad: 18] is the time from after noon until sunset, and ﴿at sunrise﴾ [Sad: 18] is after the sun rises, which is the time of forenoon. It is known that mountains are inanimate, and the inanimate is the lowest of the classes in the cosmos. Man is the lord of this cosmos and the highest of the classes, followed by animals, then plants, then inanimate things.

The True One informs us that the inanimate glorifies, and that the inanimate has life, whereas man supposes that "inanimate" means lifeless with no life in it. Yes, there is no life in it by your measure, but it has another life other than yours. You strive and move across the length and breadth of the world, whereas the inanimate is fixed and does not move.

But every kind has a life suited to it. You, O man, have two lives: a life in the state of waking, and another life in the state of sleep. Is your law while asleep the same as your law while awake? You see in sleep persons and forms, you distinguish colours, you live a long story and understand its details, all this while you are asleep with your eyes closed. By which sense did you see what you saw? After that you have another life suited to death, and another life suited to resurrection.

And if you want to prove that everything in existence has a life suited to it, then recite, if you wish: ﴿And there is not a thing but exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their exaltation...﴾ [al-Isra': 44]. Some scholars said, to escape this difficulty, that the glorification here means glorification of indication: that is, these creatures point to their Creator, and what is meant is not glorification of speech. But if the glorification meant were glorification of indication, as he says, the True One would not have said afterward: ﴿but you do not understand their exaltation﴾ [al-Isra': 44], because we understand the glorification of indication. Therefore there must be another glorification of theirs which we do not know.

Likewise in His saying about birds: ﴿And the birds in flight, each has known its prayer and its glorification﴾ [al-Nur: 41]. We have no right to investigate how the birds pray; every kind knows how to pray to Allah its Creator. Did you not see the ant when it perceived the armies of Sulayman and hastened to warn its people: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman and his soldiers crush you while they perceive not﴾ [al-Naml: 18]? Consider this caution in her words, and the justice of the judgement in ﴿while they perceive not﴾ [al-Naml: 18]. They are not oppressors nor tyrants, and if they pass over you they will crush you without knowing or perceiving you.

Did the hoopoe of Sulayman not know the matter of Tawhid? Was he not a cause of guidance for a people who had gone astray and worshipped the sun instead of Allah, when he returned to Sulayman and said: ﴿I have encompassed [knowledge] of that which you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Saba' with certain news. Indeed, I found a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne﴾ [al-Naml: 22-23].

What angered the hoopoe and affected his soul was to see them prostrating to the sun instead of Allah: ﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the way, so they are not guided. [And] that they should not prostrate to Allah, who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare﴾ [al-Naml: 24-25].

Indeed, the hoopoe understands the matter completely, and excels in it in what the rational human being does not excel.

As for the human being who boasts of the cosmos by his intellect and understanding, did not the crow teach him how to conceal the nakedness of his brother's corpse: ﴿Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal the dead body of his brother...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 31].

So every existence has its own world, its own language, and its own prayer and humility before Allah. Do not impose one law and drag it onto another law, lest you render many things impossible. If you want evidence for this from the Qur'an itself, recite His saying: ﴿That those who perished might perish upon clear evidence, and those who lived might live upon clear evidence﴾ [al-Anfal: 42]. Destruction is the opposite of life. And recite: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ [al-Qasas: 88].

So when we combine the two verses, we see that everything has a life specific to it, and although we do not grasp the true nature of this life, it exists, as proven by the fact that everything perishes. Now scientists have begun to record the language of birds and the language of animals and to arrive at decoding these languages.

Among the wonders that Allah has made to illustrate His power in His dominion is that when they built the rocket (Discovery) and wished to launch it into space, its weight being 110 tons, they found in it a defect preventing its launch. When they searched for the defect, they found a bird weighing four grams called the woodpecker, which pecked forty-two holes in the insulating wall of the fuel tank of the rocket, thereby preventing it from taking off. Thus a bird weighing four grams was made to serve, and it built its nest on this giant rocket and halted its movement.

It is as if the birds wished to avenge themselves when they saw man competing with them in the realm of flight. Therefore they found that the greatest threat to flight is the world of birds, and that flocks of them intercept aircraft and hover around airports, as though there were enmity between them and these creatures that contest them for the air.

Therefore aviation scientists thought of a scheme to drive birds away from airports. They took the idea of the calls birds emit as a warning to others when danger occurs, recorded these calls and broadcast them around the airports. But the bird noticed this trick, and these sounds no longer disturbed it. So they resorted to another means, saying that birds fear falcons, and they made models of them out of plastic and hung them up. But the birds recognised this trick too, and mocked it when some birds placed their nests on the wings of these falcons.

So the bird has its world, its kingdom and its secrets; we have known some of them, and some have remained hidden from us.

Then, when you read about our master Dawud (David), peace be upon him: ﴿Indeed, We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with him, in the evening and at sunrise﴾ [Sad 38:18]. Know that the mountains truly glorify [Allah] with a glorification that none knows except their Lord and Creator. The distinction here for Sayyidina Dawud does not lie in the glorification of the mountains, for the mountains are always glorifying; rather, the miracle here is that they glorify together with him and echo one single chant with him. So the emphasis is on "with him" (ma'ahu), meaning they glorify along with his glorification.

For this reason, we said regarding their saying "The pebbles glorified in the hand of the Messenger of Allah," we said: rephrase the expression, because the pebbles glorify even in the hand of Abu Jahl. The correct and miraculous phrasing is that we say: The Messenger of Allah heard the glorification of the pebbles in his hand. This is the greatness.

As for the meaning of ﴿in the evening..﴾ [Sad 38:18]: al-'Ashiyy is the period after midday until sunset. ﴿and at sunrise﴾ [Sad 38:18], i.e., the rising of the sun. Some of the imams have taken this verse as evidence for the legitimacy of the Duha prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā) which the Prophet (ﷺ) performed, and some of them call this prayer ṣalāt al-ishrāq (the prayer of sunrise). But which evening? And which sunrise? This is a time, and every place has an evening and a sunrise that differs from the other.

Thus: it is a time extending through every time, as we explained regarding the prayer. It is continuous and extended, never interrupted. In one place they are praying Fajr, in another they are praying Dhuhr, in another they are praying 'Asr, and so on. It is as if the Creator, glory be to Him, intended by this cycle of time that He be worshipped in every particle of time, with a worship that is never interrupted at any moment.

Among this is His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Time is never devoid of night or day." So the meaning is that His hand is always outstretched.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And the birds gathered, each one returning to Him in repentance﴾ [Sad 38:19]. The meaning of "gathered" (mahshurah) is: assembled around Sayyidina Dawud, for he, peace be upon him, had a beautiful voice when he recited the Psalms (al-mazamir) and sang them, so the birds would gather around him and echo with him and repeat what he said. Thus there was a faith-based unit composed of Sayyidina Dawud, the mountains and the birds, all of them echoing one single glorification, as if they were, as we said, one chorus.

For this reason they said regarding ﴿each one returning to Him in repentance﴾ [Sad 38:19]: that is, Dawud, the mountains and the birds, each of them is "awwab" to Allah, submissive to Him and returning to Him.

And His saying: ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾ [Sad 38:20], i.e., We made it strong and supported it with victory and awe. Victory is in everything, and awe is the strongest cause of power; therefore, when Allah wishes to weaken a king, He removes the awe of him from hearts, and when people do not fear him, they become bold against him.

﴿And We gave him wisdom and decisive speech﴾ [Sad 38:20]. Wisdom (al-hikmah): placing a thing in its appropriate place, and that from which the desired fruit comes by the shortest and easiest ways. And when the Most High uses a word among the words, He takes its intimacy from what is in the language. Thus, wisdom is derived from al-hakamah, which is the bridle placed in the jaw of a horse, so that it is easy to control and regulate its movement as desired: I loosen it so it speeds up, and I pull it so it stops.

They also said: wisdom means prophethood and soundness of judgment in matters. And both Sayyidina Dawud and Sayyidina Sulayman were distinguished in particular by Allah gathering for them both kingship and prophethood. Therefore we have seen their opponents to be (fatsanin) — there is no existence or trace of them — because kingship obliterates the violence of the opponent.

The meaning of ﴿and decisive speech﴾ [Sad 38:20] is: the knowledge of deciding between disputes. Deciding only occurs between disputants: one brings an argument and the other brings an argument, and the judge between them must decide between them, by being equitable to the truth and nullifying falsehood.

Although this matter of decisive speech has been objected to, because Sayyidina Sulayman later amended a ruling of his father, and this too is counted for Sayyidina Dawud, because the one who amended his ruling was his son, and a person does not like anyone to surpass him except his own son; therefore Sayyidina Dawud was pleased with it.

When He asks you, saying ﴿And has the story of the adversaries reached you?﴾ [Sad: 21], know that this is evidence that this matter was something you should have known. You say, "Has such-and-such reached you?" meaning: it has reached you. Similarly, His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worthy of mention?﴾ [Al-Insan: 1].

The meaning: there came upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worthy of mention. The style came in the form of a question so that you would bring out the intended meaning yourself, so that it becomes an affirmation from you. An affirmation does not constitute a lie in the way that a direct report of the intended meaning might, since a report rationally admits both truth and falsehood.

Or: this style is meant to arouse eagerness for the news (naba', news of great importance). The naba' is not just any report, but a great report that ought to be known, which is why it is given attention. Thus, telling someone, for example, "I ate such-and-such today," does not count as naba'. For this reason, when the Truthful, Glorified is He informs us about the matter of the Resurrection, He says: ﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news, about which they are in disagreement﴾ [An-Naba': 1-3].

The word ﴿al-khasm﴾ [Sad: 21] applies to the singular, the dual, and the plural in both its forms. You say: "This is a khasm (adversary), this is a khasm (fem.), these are khasm..." etc. It may also be used in the dual with a dual, as in: ﴿These two adversaries who dispute concerning their Lord﴾ [Al-Hajj: 19]. Therefore, after it comes ﴿when they climbed over the wall of the sanctuary﴾ [Sad: 21], in the plural form.

The meaning of tasawwaru is "they climbed," because they did not enter through the door; rather, they entered from the top of the wall. This is evidence that these adversaries did not come from the direction of the earth, but from the direction of the heavens, so they were a group of angels in the form of humans. The mihrab is the sacred place that a person sets aside for seclusion and for communing with his Lord. Among its uses is the saying of Exalted is He concerning Lady Maryam: ﴿Every time Zechariah entered upon her in the mihrab, he found provision with her...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 37]. We now call it the qiblah.

Then He, Glorified is He, says: ﴿When they entered upon Dawud, and he was alarmed by them﴾ [Sad: 22]. The difficulty here is: how could Sayyidna Dawud (David) be frightened by the sight of these men, when he was in the presence of Allah and under His care, before Him, praying, worshipping and glorifying Him? And how is it that the Truthful, Glorified is He, would frighten His servant and prophet while he is before Him?!

They said: fear is of two kinds. One is fear that moves your heart with anxiety while your body remains sound and unaffected. The other is fear that overflows from the heart onto the body, so that the body is affected until signs of fear appear upon it.

The fear of Sayyidna Dawud was of the second kind. Why? They said: because when the angels saw him in this state, they said to him, ﴿Do not fear﴾ [Sad: 22]. They would only say this if his body had been moved to a degree that showed fear. This is evidence that the fear had passed from his heart to his body.

We also understand from their saying to him, ﴿Do not fear﴾ [Sad: 22], that they were not among his subjects, nor were they human; for none of his subjects would dare to say to the king, "Do not fear."

Their saying: ﴿Two adversaries, one of us has wronged the other﴾ [Sad: 22] indicates their agreement despite their dispute, for they all spoke in one breath, or they spoke in turn, or one of them spoke and the rest said "Amen," and the one who says "Amen" is one of the callers. Their speaking in this orderly manner, with their hands in one another's, indicates that there is no real disagreement among them, and none of them seeks anything from the other. So, what is the matter? And what is the reality of their coming in this form? There must be another purpose for them.

The meaning of (bagha) is "tried to transgress and to oppress." ﴿So judge between us with truth, and do not deviate﴾ [Sad: 22]. This statement from them indicates their boldness, and it indicates that they are from another realm than humans, namely the angels. The meaning of ﴿do not deviate﴾ [Sad: 22] is: do not stray from the truth and do not be unjust.

﴿And guide us to the even path﴾ [Sad: 22]. "Guide us" means all of us together, without distinguishing one from another. For they were adversaries, but "even" (sawa') replaces their saying ﴿one of us has wronged the other﴾ [Sad: 22], without distinguishing the wrongdoer from the one wronged. The sirat is the straight path, and sawa' al-sirat means its middle. The meaning is: show us the truth, or the very essence of the truth. Then they began to set forth their case:

﴿Indeed, this is my brother. He has ninety-nine ewes...﴾.

Then He, glorified is He, says: when they entered upon Dawud, and he was startled by them. The difficulty here is: how could our master Dawud be startled at the sight of these people, when he was in the presence of God and under His care, standing before Him, praying, worshipping and glorifying Him? And how could the Truth, glorified is He, startle His servant and prophet while he is before Him?!!

They said: fear is of two kinds. One is a fear that moves the heart with alarm, but the body remains sound and is not affected. The other is a fear that overflows from the heart onto the body, so that the body is affected until the signs of fright appear upon it.

The fear of our master Dawud was of the second kind. Why? They said: because when the angels saw him in this state, they said to him: ﴿Do not fear﴾, and they would not say that to him unless his body had been moved in a way that showed fear. This is evidence that the fright had passed from his heart to his body.

We also understand from their saying to him ﴿Do not fear﴾ that they were not of his subjects, and not of mankind; for none of his subjects would dare to say to the king: "Do not fear."

Their saying ﴿two disputants, one of us has wronged the other﴾ indicates that they were in agreement despite their dispute, for they spoke all together in one breath, or they spoke in order, or one of them spoke and the rest said "Amen," and the one who says "Amen" is one of those who supplicate. That they spoke in this orderly manner, with their hands in one another's, indicates that there was no real enmity between them, and that none of them coveted the other. So what is the matter? And what is the reality of these people coming in this form? There must be another purpose for them.

The meaning of ﴿wronged﴾ (baghā) is: he tried to transgress and to oppress. ﴿So judge between us with truth and do not exceed the bounds﴾. This statement from them indicates their boldness, and indicates that they were of another host than mankind, namely the angels. The meaning of ﴿do not exceed the bounds﴾ (wa lā tushṭiṭ) is: do not stray from the truth and do not deviate.

﴿And guide us to the even path﴾: "guide us" means all of us, without distinguishing one from another, for they are disputants yet ﴿even﴾ (sawāʾ), as evidenced by their saying ﴿one of us has wronged the other﴾ without distinguishing the wrongdoer from the one wronged. The path (ṣirāt) is the straight road, and "the even path" (sawāʾ al-ṣirāt) means its middle. The meaning is: show us the truth, or the very essence of the truth. Then they began to set out their case: ﴿Indeed, this is my brother; he has ninety-nine ewes...﴾

In the word "brother" (*akhi*) we notice a tone of tenderness. Despite the dispute, he is still his brother, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear God?"﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 106]. This holds even in the fiercest forms of enmity, which is blood vengeance (*tha'r*). He says, glorified is He: ﴿But if anything is remitted to him by his brother﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178]. He intends to soften the heart of the guardian of the blood (*wali al-dam*) toward the killer.

The matter: ﴿Indeed, this is my brother. He has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe...﴾ [Sad: 23]. The word *na'jah* (ewe) has three uses in the language: a female sheep, a mountain goat, or a wild cow. ﴿So he said, "Give it to me to take care of"﴾ [Sad: 23]. That is, "Make it mine, and let me take care of it, for I have many sheep. Let it graze with my sheep, so one shepherd will suffice us instead of you having to hire a shepherd for it." The meaning is that its guardianship is easy for me and does not burden me with anything.

﴿And he overcame me in speech﴾ [Sad: 23]. That is, he overpowered me with argument and debate. It is well known that a judge rules by proof and evidence. Our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), says:

The meaning is that my brother overpowered me with his speech and his mastery of his argument, and I feel wronged and my soul is not content. Therefore I came to you to raise my matter to you so that you may judge it. Thus David (peace be upon him) heard the claim of the first party and did not hear the other side, and this is one of the lapses of a judge.

For this reason, the people of knowledge (*ahl al-ma'rifah*) said regarding this issue: If a claimant comes to you whose eye has been gouged out, do not rule in his favor until you have heard from the other party, for perhaps his eyes have been gouged out too. Our master David hastened to rule, and said:

﴿He said, "He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe in addition to his own ewes..."﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 38, verse 24:

His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ﴾ ("He has certainly wronged you"). He attributed wrongdoing to one party by ﴿بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِ﴾ ("by demanding your ewe be added to his ewes"). He introduced something into the basis of the judgment that is not part of the basis of the judgment.
